# "Retention Architecture" — General Counsel's Briefing

**[Verse 1 — The Clean Framework]**

Listen up, team, let me walk you through the stack,
Our Right-to-Be-Forgotten portal — fully GDPR-backed,
Standard intake form, identity verification layer,
Data subject sends a request, we process it — no prayer,
For Category One content — that's consumer-facing data —
We run a balancing test, proportionality, see you later,
Public interest weighting, journalistic exemption check,
Legitimate purpose analysis — everything correct,
Response time: thirty days, with a fourteen-day extension,
Denial rate's at forty percent — withstands regulatory inspection,
We log every determination, keep the audit trail pristine,
On paper? Textbook compliance. Cleanest you've ever seen.

**[Verse 2 — The Expanded Classification]**

Now Category Two — this is where the architecture bends,
Internal-origin content — that's where our *special schema* extends,
See, any safety incident report names an *employee*,
And an employee name is PII — that's Article Four, Subsection One-A to me,
So when a request comes in — and we *generate* those requests,
Through annual privacy preference reviews we quietly suggest —
The deletion scope cascades: you pull the employee name,
But the report's now "orphaned data," contextually defamed,
Our classification engine flags it: "mixed personal-operational,"
And our policy says mixed records get the *personal* jurisdictional
Treatment — so the whole document enters the deletion queue,
Not because we're hiding anything — we're protecting personnel, boo.

**[Verse 3 — The Differential Engine]**

Here's the elegance — the differential treatment's *procedural*,
Consumer data gets the standard test — adversarial, contextual,
But internal docs? We added a "dignity impact score,"
Proprietary metric, weighted toward deletion — nothing more,
Any record where an employee *could* be re-identified,
Even with the names redacted — "mosaic risk," we've certified,
Gets flagged for "enhanced privacy processing," which in practice means
The retention period drops from seven years to just thirteen
Months — and wouldn't you know, most regulatory lookbacks
Run twenty-four — so by the time an auditor attacks,
The incident reports, the near-miss logs, the internal safety reviews,
Have aged out of the system. Legally? *We didn't choose* —
The *automated retention policy* made the disposition call,
We just built the classification rules. We didn't delete at all.

**[Verse 4 — The Firewall]**

And if a regulator asks why safety data's running thin,
We point them to our privacy-by-design certification win,
We show the DPA our deletion logs — all procedurally sound,
Every action tied to a data-subject request we *found*,
The privacy office and the safety office? Separate reporting lines,
Chinese wall between them — safety can't see privacy's designs,
So the safety team just thinks the records aged out naturally,
And privacy just thinks they're following the framework factually,
No single person holds the full picture — that's the point,
Compartmentalization means no whistleblower to anoint,
The architecture *is* the strategy, the policy *is* the shield,
And if it ever hits a courtroom? We *complied*. Case sealed.
